concept.anti_generic_signature: The model must preserve the four-coupled-axle 2-8-0 stance visible in the exact 1888 photograph, a compact Class 60-informed boiler-to-cab relationship, flared diamond stack, square kerosene headlamp carrying 100, and Silverton tender proportion; generic steam-train proportions fail even if decorated correctly. Numerical spacing remains provisional until the GA gate passes.
assumptions: A provenance-verified period side/front/cab-rear GA applicable to No. 100 or its documented D&RG donor components can be obtained; the circulating personal-use reproduction is not authority and must not be traced unless that provenance is established.

The NPS sister Class 60/C-16 record's 36 in driver is a viable Invent target for No. 100's 1887 rebuild; Make must test that inference and the composite D&RG component history against the GA and exact photograph.
The sealed 174.0 x 31.0 x 47.0 mm envelope will remain consistent with the verified GA; if it does not, Make returns the contradiction to Invent rather than changing dependent parameters.
The model is a flat-desk free roller, not a claim of compatibility with commercial HOn3 track, turnouts, or electrical pickup.

build_plan.exit_criteria: First acquire and record a provenance-verified period side/front/cab-rear GA applicable either to No. 100 itself or to its documented D&RG Class 60 donor components, then reconcile it with the exact 1888 photograph. If the GA contradicts the sealed 10.51 mm datum, four 11.0 mm axle pitches, or 174 x 31 x 47 mm envelope materially, stop Make and return that design-blocking evidence to Invent; do not silently rewrite parameters. If consistent, persist the three-clearance journal coupon and one-journal frame strip before detailing. The complete locomotive must have 0.20 mm modeled radial journal clearance, 360 degree digital wheel rotation, retained pilot axle and pivot, and a source-overlay report; physical rolling remains unclaimed.

The two separate four-wheel trucks each yaw 8 degrees around a retained 3.0/3.4 mm pivot and their four axles each have 0.20 mm modeled radial clearance with 360 degree digital rotation. Independently gauged fleet interfaces must show the locomotive's pilot-front and engine-rear hooks accepting the 2.0 mm tender bars in 2.4 mm openings at Z=7.0 mm, including 12 degrees locomotive-to-tender yaw. Lettering is 1.8 mm high with 0.8 mm strokes, the assembly stays inside 174 x 31 x 47 mm, and every part slices support-disabled; physical fit, rolling, and coupling remain unclaimed.

concept.coordinate_system: Model millimetres. X=0 at the pilot tip and increases toward the tender rear; Y=0 is the longitudinal center plane; Z=0 is the flat-desk standing plane. Wheel treads touch Z=0. Each inboard flange is a 0.6 mm axial side-face relief whose outer diameter equals the tread diameter, so no flange projects below the standing plane.
detail_grading: Keep the provisional 10.51 mm drivers, 7.0 mm pilot wheels, 7.59 mm tender wheels, diamond stack outline, dome line, pilot bars, box headlamp, cab windows, tender flare, two-truck underframe, and wheel spacing as silhouette geometry subject to the GA source gate.
Represent handrails and fixed side rods as attached 0.8 x 0.8 mm ribs; they are not separate wires and do not move. Side-rod relief clears rotating wheel faces by 0.4 mm.
Represent rivet rows as 0.8 mm diameter by 0.3 mm high surface bosses only where the period sheet or exact photograph supports a row; omit isolated sub-0.8 mm fasteners.

Render SILVERTON R.R. CO. as process-resolved 1.8 mm cap-height raised block letters with 0.8 mm minimum stroke and 0.4 mm relief. This is an explicitly enlarged readability treatment; placement follows the period elevation.
Render headlamp 100 as 1.6 mm cap-height recessed digits with 0.8 mm minimum stroke and 0.4 mm depth; omit unreadable builder-plate text.
No functional valve gear, brake rigging, cab interior, piping below 0.8 mm, individual coal lumps, electronics, or lighting. Record each omission in the manual.
concept.hardest_to_fake_magic: A knowledgeable viewer recognizes the Silverton Railroad's 1887 composite rebuild as photographed in 1888 from a neutral side silhouette reconciled to that exact photograph and a provenance-verified period GA, while the same small object is engineered to roll and couple as a fleet piece.
concept.interaction: The owner assembles the four driver wheelsets behind the sliding locomotive keeper, captures the pilot axle with its own keeper, pins the swiveling pilot truck to the frame, and adds the boiler, dome cluster, diamond stack, cab, headlamp, and pilot beam. The tender tank seats on its frame while two separately printed four-wheel trucks pivot below it, each with its own axle keeper. The locomotive's integral rear hook lowers over the tender's front transverse bar; the integral pilot-front hook and tender-rear transverse bar preserve the Ferro Line hook/bar polarity at both outside ends. A fingertip push is intended to rotate all nine wheelsets on a flat desk; Make must prove or falsify that behavior. Recognition comes from the 2-8-0 wheel spacing, diamond-stack profile, box headlamp marked 100, and SILVERTON R.R. CO. tender rather than packaging text.

make_falsification_proof.causal_geometry: A 28.0 x 18.0 x 12.0 mm strip containing one 3.4 mm split journal, the keeper rail, and one 10.51 mm driver/3.0 mm axle is the cheapest exact test. It fails the chosen running system if digital clearance is below 0.15 mm anywhere, if the wheel cannot rotate 360 degrees, if the keeper cannot be installed along X, or if a support-disabled slice requires internal support or leaves the external axle fin inaccessible.
make_falsification_proof.clearance_coupon: One coupon carries 3.0 mm axle and dovetail pairs at 0.20, 0.25, and 0.30 mm per-side clearance plus the 0.4 x 0.8 mm bed-edge relief. Digital checks choose none as physically proven; the coupon exists so one later print can select a real process fit.
make_falsification_proof.held_view_blockout: A neutral unlettered assembly blockout at 1:87 in left-front three-quarter view must show the locomotive as a compact engineered object that can be grasped under frame and tender, with no stack, lamp, pilot bar, or hook thinner than the stated process floor.
make_falsification_proof.signature_view_blockout: A neutral orthographic left-side blockout must reconcile the exact 1888 photograph with a provenance-verified applicable period GA and test four equal 10.51 mm drivers on 11.0 mm pitch, the leading truck, boiler/cab balance, diamond stack, box headlamp, two tender trucks, and separate tender before rivets or lettering are added. A material source contradiction blocks Make and returns to Invent.

novel_mechanisms.definition: A serviceable all-printed running system in which each fused wheel-and-axle part rotates in a 3.4 mm split journal closed by a longitudinal sliding keeper; the 3.0 mm axle has 0.20 mm radial design clearance and no elastic latch or purchased bearing.

The Ferro Line rail interface with fixed polarity: the locomotive carries integral 1.6 mm thick hooks with 2.4 mm openings at its pilot-front and engine-rear ends; the tender carries removable 2.0 mm diameter transverse bars at its front and rear ends. Every coupling center is 7.0 mm above the desk and 3.0 mm behind its vehicle end face.

print_stance.bed_edge_relief: Every bed-facing mating perimeter receives a 0.4 mm horizontal by 0.8 mm vertical chamfer, excluding wheel treads and visible lettering faces.
print_stance.minimums: Rigid walls 1.6 mm, frame load paths 2.0 mm, freestanding features 0.8 mm, attached surface relief 0.4 mm high by 0.8 mm wide, handled-edge fillets or chamfers 0.4 mm.
print_stance.orientation: Frame, keepers, truck frames, pivot pins, and coupling bars lie on their broad or split-prototype faces; wheelsets print with axle axes parallel to the bed, both treads tangent to the bed, and one externally graspable 0.4 mm breakaway fin below each axle; boiler stands on the smokebox face; cab stands on its rear wall; diamond stack stands inverted on its 18.0 mm cap; tender tank stands on its rear wall; pilot and headlamp use their prototype seam faces as beds.
print_stance.overhang_rule: All hidden bore crowns use 45 degree teardrops and every visible downward face is reshaped to 45 degrees or split at a prototype seam. The only designed support is one externally graspable 0.4 mm axle fin per wheelset; no slicer support, internal support, or trapped breakaway lattice is permitted.
print_stance.process: 0.4 mm nozzle FDM; 0.20 mm layers; supports disabled for qualification.

risks: Exact No. 100 archive drawing provenance and reuse rights are unresolved at Invent. Make cannot pass the source gate using the rejected Clipart Library copy; failure to secure an applicable provenance-verified period GA is a truthful Make blocker.

A 3.0 mm horizontally printed axle with a removable support fin can remain rough or weak in some FDM processes; the three-clearance coupon, fin-removal inspection, and one-journal early proof must precede all wheel detailing.
The 18.0 mm diamond-stack cap and 1.6 mm hollow walls can warp; Make must compare inverted and split-at-seam print stances without altering the visible profile.
Process-enlarged lettering is intentionally not exact scale thickness; its position and words are faithful while its stroke is graded to the nozzle.
Digital clearance proves absence of modeled collision, not physical rolling, friction, fit, durability, or first-layer release.

scale_and_datum.envelope_status: The 174.0 x 31.0 x 47.0 mm assembled target is a deliberate provisional envelope inferred from Class 60 proportions, not a measured No. 100 dimension. Make may proceed only if a provenance-verified period GA is consistent with it; a material contradiction returns to Invent rather than being silently rewritten.
scale_and_datum.gauge: 10.5 mm between tread contact center planes at Y=-5.25 and Y=+5.25 mm, representing 914.4 mm three-foot gauge at 1:87 within 0.01 mm. Every wheel body is 2.0 mm axially thick; its 0.6 mm inboard flange relief lies beyond the inner wheel face but shares the tread outer diameter.
scale_and_datum.provisional_datum: 36.0 in sister Class 60/C-16 driver diameter becomes 10.51 mm at 1:87. This is a sealed Invent target, not an exact No. 100 measurement; Make must test it against a provenance-verified period GA and report a design-blocking contradiction instead of silently editing the target.

concept.signature_interaction: The intended result is that a fingertip push turns all nine wheelsets beneath a silhouette that reads as No. 100 before the raised tender lettering is read; the one-journal proof and full digital rotation check must establish this before any success claim.
concept.summary: A 1:87, all-FDM, support-aware desk-running reconstruction concept for Silverton Railroad No. 100 “Ouray,” the railroad's 1887 composite rebuild from Baldwin-built D&RG components: four coupled 10.51 mm driver wheelsets under a low Class 60 frame, a compact boiler and Victorian cab crowned by a diamond stack, a box headlamp and pilot, and a separately rolling tender on two swiveling four-wheel trucks with process-resolved SILVERTON R.R. CO. lettering. The exact 1888 Fort Lewis photograph establishes identity and wheel arrangement; sister Class 60/C-16 records provisionally bound dimensions. A provenance-verified period GA remains a mandatory first Make gate, so no exact-drawing fidelity is claimed at Invent. No motor, light, metal axle, purchased bearing, or commercial-kit geometry enters the design.
concept.title: Ferro Line 1:87 No. 100 “Ouray” — 1887 Silverton Railroad composite 2-8-0

vault_lead_responses.response: Make applies 0.4 x 0.8 mm bed-edge relief to mating perimeters and first authors the exact 0.20/0.25/0.30 mm clearance coupon. Wheel treads are excluded from relief. No physical first-layer or release claim is made.

Every part has a deliberate show face: boiler seam goes under the running board, cab seam on the rear wall bed face, tender seam on its rear wall, stack seam under the cap, and wheel seams on inboard faces. Make must inspect shaded renders and exact slicer seam placement before sealing.

Freestanding features are at least 0.8 mm; surface relief is at least 0.4 mm high by 0.8 mm wide; tender letters use 1.8 mm caps and 0.8 mm strokes; sub-floor pipework, builder-plate text, and isolated fasteners are explicitly omitted. Make must run a 0.8 mm process-floor audit on exact meshes and toolpaths.

The design uses no snap beam or elastic latch. Journal keepers slide along broad XY-printed dovetail rails; frame axle loads pass through 2.0 mm continuous webs; stack and superstructure pins load in compression or shear. Physical strength and fatigue remain unverified.

Prototype construction seams isolate boiler, cab, fittings, pilot, frame, and tender. Bores use 45 degree teardrop crowns, downward faces are limited to 45 degrees, and each horizontal wheelset uses one externally graspable 0.4 mm designed fin. No slicer support, internal support, or trapped sacrificial lattice is permitted. Make must obtain a warning-free support-disabled slice and visible fin-removal evidence.

Rigid shells are 1.6 mm, frame and chassis load paths are 2.0 mm, running boards are 1.6 mm, and local roof/edge members are 2.0 mm. Make must map and pass the declared wall-duty ledger at full 1.6/2.0 mm duties rather than checking only the 0.8 mm process floor.
